title: When StringBuilder is preferable to StringBuffer
answer: `StringBuilder` is preferable when mutable text is confined to one thread or one method and does not need synchronized access. It offers the same basic append, insert, delete, and reverse style of operations without the synchronization overhead of `StringBuffer`. In AeroTopo, `SurveyAlgorithms.reverse` and `expandRuns` create local `StringBuilder` instances that are not shared across threads, so `StringBuilder` is the appropriate choice. `StringBuffer` is mainly relevant when one mutable character buffer is genuinely shared by multiple threads and synchronized method access is required.

steps.question: AeroTopo's `reverse` method creates a `StringBuilder` locally, reverses the supplied comment, and immediately converts the result back to String; The builder never escapes the method or becomes shared state; Why does this thread-confined usage make synchronization unnecessary and therefore favor `StringBuilder` over `StringBuffer`.
steps.why_te: SurveyAlgorithms; reverse lo builder local method variable; Vere thread tho share kaadu; Synchronization avasaram ledu kabatti StringBuilder simple and appropriate choice.

steps.question: `expandRuns` also creates a local `StringBuilder` and repeatedly appends generated text while decoding an input sequence; Because one invocation owns its builder from creation to return, what concurrency problem would a synchronized `StringBuffer` solve here that the method does not actually have.
steps.why_te: expandRuns lo kuda builder each method call ki local ga create avutundi; Shared mutable state ledu; StringBuffer synchronization ikkada solve cheyyalsina concurrency problem emi ledu.

steps.title: Connect the choice to thread confinement rather than class popularity
steps.question: The important decision is not that `StringBuilder` is universally better; it is that synchronization should match the ownership model; If one mutable buffer were genuinely shared and modified concurrently by several threads, why would `StringBuffer` become more relevant even though local builders remain preferable for ordinary method-scoped work.
steps.why_te: Choice ownership model batti untundi; Local single-thread buffer ki StringBuilder enough; Same mutable buffer multiple threads share chesthe synchronized StringBuffer relevant avvachu.

steps.why_te: Loop lo repeated append jarugutundi; Immutable String concatenation repeated ga intermediate values create cheyyachu; Local StringBuilder same mutable buffer lo content accumulate chestundi.
